analysis:
Examined both BASE excerpts of docs/provider/cli-reference.md, covering Autopilot consent/build verification (1188–1240), sandbox installation and subprocess contracts (1324–1611), and lifecycle, uninstall and serving diagnostics (1613–1982). Compared the complete changed-range map and bounded patch with the canonical index and supplied T-041 detail. The visible patch adds a sandbox waitlist approval requirement at head line 182; it does not establish an authorization bypass or other concrete regression. BASE already downloads and executes the installer for planning before installation confirmation (1381–1415), so that behavior is not a new finding (TB-013/T-061, A-019). BASE uninstall preserves keys and external caches (1806–1835); T-041 distinguishes ciphertext retention from cryptographic purge, and no change to those controls is shown. Drain, token revocation and fresh restart authorization are surrounding unchanged contracts relevant to A-008/T-053; no regression is established here.
Coverage limit: these units contain BASE documentation, not the replacement setup steps or new head section at 1635–1727. Integration must examine those HEAD sections and any supplied implementation to determine whether waitlist approval gates installer download/execution or only enrollment, and how refusal/continuation interacts with repair and already-installed states (BASE 1475–1501). Validate that new service responses cannot authorize owner-account execution or disclose credentials beyond the intended sandbox boundary. Missing HEAD/source evidence prevents concluding that the changed approval workflow preserves TB-013/T-061; it is not itself evidence of a vulnerability.
